headline: Hackers dump 421,000 alleged AfD emails and the party confirms a breach; a Google Cloud zone in London knocks out UK banks; Amazon pledges €16bn for Germany; the EU Parliament's centre agrees to soften the combustion-engine ban; Zelensky meets Witkoff in Oslo.

stories.title: About 421,000 alleged AfD emails are online, and the party confirms a hack
facts: Unknown actors published what they say are 421,179 AfD emails (281 GB) from 10 inboxes, including one in Alexander Gauland's name and an old national-HQ contact address.
The AfD confirms a September 2026 attack on a hosting provider; it says parts of a few mostly long-unused inboxes were copied and current federal accounts weren't affected.
Authenticity is still unverified; Bild says the material it saw includes ID photos, invoices, bank statements and membership lists from NRW district branches.
Bild reports mails attributed to Alice Weidel are in the dump, though her own account apparently wasn't hacked.
Lilith Wittmann on X: she doesn't yet know of a single newsroom that can fully search the material.
stories.whyItMatters: The dump includes members' personal data, so expect slow, contested verification; treat early claims about what the mails show with care.

stories.title: A Google Cloud zone in London goes down and takes UK banks and apps with it
facts: Google's status page: elevated errors and intermittent network failures in europe-west2 since 08:08 Berlin time; dozens of products are listed as impacted.
The Register: zone europe-west2-b failed; Lloyds, HSBC, Royal Mail and Revolut were hit, with no recovery time and "no workarounds for now".
The BBC is running a live page as bank customers report problems.
ClickHouse Cloud says only zone B is affected and it is moving workloads out of it.
stories.whyItMatters: One availability zone shouldn't take out a bank; the outage shows how many UK services run without real multi-zone failover.

stories.title: Amazon pledges more than €16bn for Germany in 2027 at Merz's investment summit
facts: Announced at the government's Invest in Germany Summit in Berlin; it covers data centers and AI, Amazon Leo satellite internet, logistics and Prime Video productions.
€4.8bn of it goes to expanding AWS's Frankfurt region; Hesse frames it as data centers across Rhine-Main.
Amazon is also opening a second robotics and AI research lab in Berlin.
Amazon says it has invested more than €100bn and created over 40,000 permanent jobs in Germany since 2010.
Handelsblatt: around 200 investors are at the summit at ESMT in Berlin-Mitte.
stories.whyItMatters: It's the first big number to come out of the summit after this morning's Nvidia pact, and it makes Leo a European rival to Starlink.

stories.title: The EU Parliament's centre agrees to soften the 2035 combustion-engine ban
facts: EPP, S&D and Renew negotiators agreed overnight: new cars must cut CO₂ 95% from 2021 levels by 2035, or only 87.5% if they use green steel.
That keeps new combustion and hybrid cars sellable after 2035 without fines for carmakers.
It's not final yet: the transport and industry committees vote Thursday, the environment committee in early November, and the plenary in December.
It follows last week's Merz–Macron deal (a 90% cut with no compensation required), which is seen as setting the line for the Council.
Transport & Environment calls the Franco-German deal a "historic mistake" for climate goals and for Europe's car industry.

stories.title: Zelensky meets Witkoff in Oslo as Trump floats a nuclear summit with Xi and Putin
facts: Zelensky met US envoy Steve Witkoff in Oslo, with Jared Kushner on video and Finland's Stubb and Norway's Støre present, ahead of Witkoff's planned talks with Putin in Moscow (Euronews).
Before that he spoke with Marco Rubio about ballistic-missile interceptors, early warning of Russian strikes and restoring Starlink/Starshield.
AP: a Russian missile and drone barrage killed 7 people in Ukraine.
Trump says he is open to a three-way meeting with Xi and Putin on denuclearization at the APEC summit in Shenzhen on Nov 18–19.
China calls joining trilateral disarmament talks "neither fair, reasonable nor realistic"; Ukraine's foreign minister says a Putin–Xi–Trump meeting would only encourage the war.
stories.whyItMatters: This is the follow-up to this morning's interceptor story: Kyiv is lobbying Washington directly while Moscow tries to set up a summit without it.

Waymo is coming to Madrid, its first region in Spain and second in the EU, with fully driverless ride-hailing planned for 2027.
DAX around 25,075 at midday, almost 1% lower, weighed down by AI and tech stocks.
Microsoft announced new Sovereign Cloud capabilities in Paris for sensitive workloads in public and private cloud.
Australian police charge a man over what they call a "targeted" attack on MP Helen Haines, who remains in critical condition.
Blackwall raises $100M at a $2.2B valuation for tools that filter bot and AI traffic on websites.
